arxiv-2106-13119.title: The moment polytope of the abelian polygon space Thanks: Both the authors are partially supported by a grant from the Infosys foundation. The project is also supported by the second author’s MATRICS grant funded by the Science and Engineering Board, Government of India.
arxiv-2106-13119.creator: Navnath Daundkar, Priyavrat Deshpande
arxiv-2106-13119.description: Abstract . The moduli space of n n chains in the plane with generic side lengths that terminate on a fixed line is a smooth, closed manifold of dimension n − 1 n-1 . This manifold is also equipped with a locally standard action of ℤ 2 n − 1 \mathbb{Z}_{2}^{n-1} .

arxiv-2202-07489.title: Generalized uncertainty principle and quantum non-locality
arxiv-2202-07489.creator: 1 S. Aghababaei, 2 H. Moradpour
arxiv-2202-07489.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by 1 S. Aghababaei, 2 H. Moradpour. The emergence of the generalized uncertainty principle and the existence of a non-zero minimal length are intertwined. On the other hand, the Heisenberg uncertainty principle forms the core of the EPR paradox.

arxiv-2205-01668.title: End-to-End Visual Editing with a Generatively Pre-Trained Artist
arxiv-2205-01668.creator: Andrew Brown, Cheng-Yang Fu, Omkar Parkhi, Tamara L. Berg, Andrea Vedaldi
arxiv-2205-01668.description: Abstract We consider the targeted image editing problem: blending a region in a source image with a driver image that specifies the desired change. Differently from prior works, we solve this problem by learning a conditional probability distribution of the edits, end-to-end . Training such a model requires addressing a fundamental technical challenge: the lack of example edits for training.

arxiv-2206-15064.title: Cluster Random Fields and Random-Shift Representations
arxiv-2206-15064.creator: Enkelejd Hashorva
arxiv-2206-15064.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Enkelejd Hashorva. Abstract: Cluster random fields (CRFs) play a crucial role in the study of extremes of stationary regularly varying random fields (RFs). In particular, they appear in the Rosiński representation of max-stable and \alpha -stable RFs. In this contribution we introduce CRFs in an abstract setting proving that they are crucial for the construction of shift-generated classes of \alpha -homogeneous RFs. Further, we investigate the relations between CRFs, tail RFs and spectral tail RFs .

arxiv-2411-06817.title: Ultrastrong coupling, nonselective measurement and quantum Zeno dynamics
arxiv-2411-06817.creator: Stefano Marcantoni, Marco Merkli
arxiv-2411-06817.description: Abstract We study the dynamics of an open quantum system linearly coupled to a bosonic reservoir. We show that, in the ultrastrong coupling limit, the system undergoes a nonselective measurement and then evolves unitarily according to an effective Zeno Hamiltonian. This dynamical process is largely independent of the reservoir state.

arxiv-2504-05635.title: The L p L^{p} -boundedness of wave operators for nonhomogeneous fourth-order Schrödinger operators in high dimensions Thanks: The work is partially supported by NSFC No. 12171182
arxiv-2504-05635.creator: Zijun Wan, Xiaohua Yao
arxiv-2504-05635.description: Abstract . This paper investigates the L p L^{p} -boundedness of wave operators associated with the following nonhomogeneous fourth-order Schödinger operator on ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} : H = Δ 2 − Δ + V ⁡ ( x ) . H=\Delta^{2}-\Delta+V(x).

arxiv-2507-02084.title: Adaptive Iterative Soft-Thresholding Algorithm with the Median Absolute Deviation
arxiv-2507-02084.creator: Yining Feng, and Ivan Selesnick
arxiv-2507-02084.description: Abstract The adaptive Iterative Soft-Thresholding Algorithm (ISTA) has been a popular algorithm for finding a desirable solution to the LASSO problem without explicitly tuning the regularization parameter λ \lambda . Despite that the adaptive ISTA is a successful practical algorithm, few theoretical results exist.

arxiv-2510-17114.title: Towards Imperceptible Watermarking Via Environment Illumination for Consumer Cameras
arxiv-2510-17114.creator: Hodaka Kawachi, Tomoya Nakamura, Hiroaki Santo, SaiKiran Kumar Tedla, Trevor Dalton Canham, Yasushi Yagi, Michael S. Brown, [2pt] University of Osaka
arxiv-2510-17114.description: Abstract This paper introduces a method for using LED-based environmental lighting to produce visually imperceptible watermarks for consumer cameras. Our approach optimizes an LED light source’s spectral profile to be minimally visible to the human eye while remaining highly detectable by typical consumer cameras.

arxiv-2510-26745.title: Deep sequence models tend to memorize geometrically; it is unclear why.
arxiv-2510-26745.creator: Shahriar Noroozizadeh, Vaishnavh Nagarajan, Elan Rosenfeld, Sanjiv Kumar
arxiv-2510-26745.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shahriar Noroozizadeh, Vaishnavh Nagarajan, Elan Rosenfeld, Sanjiv Kumar. In sequence modeling, the parametric memory of atomic facts has been predominantly abstracted as a brute-force lookup of co-occurrences between entities. We contrast this associative view against a geometric view of how memory is stored. We begin by isolating a clean and analyzable instance of Transformer reasoning that is incompatible with memory as strictly a storage of the local co-occurrences specified during training.

arxiv-2511-02900.title: Clifford Hierarchy Stabilizer Codes: Transversal Non-Clifford Gates and Magic
arxiv-2511-02900.creator: Ryohei Kobayashi, Guanyu Zhu, Po-Shen Hsin
arxiv-2511-02900.description: Abstract A fundamental problem in fault-tolerant quantum computation is the tradeoff between universality and dimensionality, exemplified by the the Bravyi-König bound for n n -dimensional topological stabilizer codes. In this work, we extend topological Pauli stabilizer codes to a broad class of n n -dimensional Clifford hierarchy stabilizer codes.

arxiv-2511-11669.title: H-Model: Dynamic Neural Architectures for Adaptive Processing
arxiv-2511-11669.creator: Dmytro Hospodarchuk
arxiv-2511-11669.description: Abstract This article explores the design and experimentation of a neural network architecture capable of dynamically adjusting its internal structure based on the input data. The proposed model introduces a routing mechanism that allows each layer to influence how its outputs are propagated through the network, enabling iterative and adaptive computation.

legge-chinese-classics-vol-5-part-2-1872.title: The Chinese Classics, Vol. 5, Part 2: The Ch'un Ts'ew (Spring and Autumn Annals)
legge-chinese-classics-vol-5-part-2-1872.creator: James Legge (trans.)
legge-chinese-classics-vol-5-part-2-1872.description: Vol. 5 Part 2 of Legge's Chinese Classics. Full text, public domain.

pmc-10775733.title: Endocrine-disrupting chemicals and epigenetic reprogramming in developmental origin of uterine fibroids
pmc-10775733.creator: Qiwei Yang, Mohamed Ali, Maria Victoria Bariani, Somayeh Vafaei, Ayman Al-Hendy
pmc-10775733.description: Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) are a class of exogenous substances that mimic the effects of hormones in the body, inducing hormonal dysregulation and contributing to various disorders. Epigenome regulation has emerged as an important mechanism for maintaining organ function in health and disease.

pmc-11459380.title: TrajectoryGeometry suggests cell fate decisions can involve branches rather than bifurcations
pmc-11459380.creator: Anna Laddach, Vassilis Pachnis, Michael Shapiro
pmc-11459380.description: Differentiation of multipotential progenitor cells is a key process in the development of any multi-cellular organism and often continues throughout its life. It is often assumed that a bi-potential progenitor develops along a (relatively) straight trajectory until it reaches a decision point where the trajectory bifurcates.

pmc-11693173.title: THE CONNECTION BETWEEN SEROTONIN SIGNALING, AGING, AND IMMUNITY WHEN OBSERVED FROM C. ELEGANS AND HUMAN STUDIES
pmc-11693173.creator: Liyat Kebbede, Brandy Weathers, Tripti Nair
pmc-11693173.description: As humans age, various environmental threats impact healthspan. Therefore maintaining an intact immune system is vital. Efficiency of human immune response can decline over time leading to complications with age-related diseases. Homeostatic mechanisms are in place to combat threats to the immune system.

pmc-11698367.title: The dawn and twilight of Old Irish scholarship
pmc-11698367.creator: David Stifter
pmc-11698367.description: Even though the publication of Johann Kaspar Zeuss’s monumental Grammatica Celtica (Zeuss 1853) marks the beginning of the modern, scientific study of the Old Irish language, short excerpts of the most important textual witnesses of Old Irish, the so-called Old Irish glosses, preserved in 8th–9th-century manuscripts on the European Continent, had appeared in print since the early 18th century.

pmc-11713754.title: Development of AI‐4‐AD tools for evaluation and prognosis of AD conversion: multi‐branch network and multi‐task deep learning algorism
pmc-11713754.creator: Liang Han, Ran Pang, Qing Ren, Xiujuan Pu, Yuan Liu, Yuanfan Tan, Qing X Yang
pmc-11713754.description: BackgroundAD prevention and early interventions require tools for evaluation of people during aging for diagnosis and prognosis of AD conversion. Since AD is a complicated continuum of neurodegenerative processes, developing of such tools have been difficult because it needs longitudinal and multimodal data which are often complicated and incomplete.

pmc-12427508.title: Synergistic Effects of Novel Xanthone Derivatives and Mild Hyperthermia in Ovarian Cancer: Insights from Gene Expression and In Silico Analyses
pmc-12427508.creator: Jakub Rech, Dorota Żelaszczyk, Henryk Marona, Ilona Anna Bednarek
pmc-12427508.description: Simple SummaryOvarian cancer treatments often focus on novel derivatives of existing substances. This study examines xanthone derivatives combined with mild hyperthermia on TOV-21G and SK-OV-3 ovarian cancer cell lines. We analyzed the expression of 84 stress-related genes, including anti-oxidant/pro-oxidant enzymes, molecular chaperones, and xenobiotic metabolism including the cytochrome P450 group. In silico analyses, gene pathways, enrichment, and ontology were explored.

pmc-12570727.title: Functional prognosis of older adults with tetanus in Japan: a single-center retrospective study
pmc-12570727.creator: Takeru Yamamoto, Ryuichi Minoda Sada, Shungo Yamamoto, Ryosuke Osawa, Naoto Hosokawa, Satoshi Kutsuna
pmc-12570727.description: BackgroundGlobally tetanus causes 26,000–48,000 deaths annually, mostly in children in lower and middle-income countries. In Japan, approximately 100 cases of tetanus are diagnosed annually, mostly in older adults. However, information on the functional prognosis of tetanus in older adults in high-income countries is limited. Therefore, this study assessed the functional prognosis of adults hospitalized with tetanus in Japan.

pmc-12652634.title: Single-Cell Multi-Omics in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Revealing Cellular Heterogeneity and Mechanistic Insights
pmc-12652634.creator: Yijie Wei, Feitong Hong, Sijia Xie, Xinwei Luo, Xiaolong Li, Fuying Dao, Kejun Deng, Hao Lin, Hao Lyu, Ana Amić
pmc-12652634.description: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a prevalent and complex metabolic disorder characterized by insulin resistance, progressive β-cell dysfunction, and severe systemic complications. Advances in single-cell multi-omics—transcriptomics, chromatin accessibility profiling, and integrative analyses—have offered unprecedented insights into the cellular heterogeneity and regulatory networks of pancreatic islets.

pmc-12695789.title: Targeting innate and adaptive immunity to suppress lung cancer metastasis
pmc-12695789.creator: Rong Qin
pmc-12695789.description: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality globally, with metastasis and recurrence as the primary determinants of poor prognosis. Despite advances in immunotherapy, intrinsic and acquired resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) underscores the need to explore alternative immunomodulatory strategies.

pmc-13083147.title: How university physical education instructors’ political literacy shapes student values: the mediating role of teacher educative efficacy in the Chinese context
pmc-13083147.creator: Xiao Qiaoli, Liu Bing
pmc-13083147.description: BackgroundIn the context of China’s comprehensive implementation of the fundamental task of “Fostering Virtue through Education,” integrating values education into university physical education (PE) and elevating it from “skill delivery” to “character shaping” has become a central educational issue of China. However, robust empirical evidence on how PE instructors’ political literacy drives this process remains scarce.

pmc-13254109.title: A hierarchical neuromorphic multi agent framework for energy aware and secure 6G resource optimization using Neuro6G agent
pmc-13254109.creator: Ahmed Al Nuaim, Junaid Qayyum
pmc-13254109.description: The convergence of Sixth-Generation (6G) wireless networks and neuromorphic computing presents significant opportunities for intelligent, energy-efficient resource management in distributed architectures. This paper introduces Neuro6G-Agent, a hierarchical neuromorphic agentic intelligence framework that integrates Energy-Aware Spiking Neural Networks (EA-SNNs) with multi-agent reinforcement learning to enable energy-conscious cognitive collaboration across cloud-edge-end 6G deployments.

pmc-13292640.title: Maternal smoking during pregnancy, other reproductive factors, and neonatal jaundice: A two-sample Mendelian randomization study
pmc-13292640.creator: Wenjing Geng, Donge Feng, Jingbin Qian

pmc-13421587.title: A detailed investigation of a-IGZO thin film-based MSM UV photodetector
pmc-13421587.creator: Tarik Asar
pmc-13421587.description: Amorphous Indium–Gallium–Zinc–Oxide (a-IGZO) thin films were deposited on silicon and glass substrates using a magnetron sputtering system at room temperature. The structural, morphological, optical, and electrical properties of the films were systematically investigated to evaluate their suitability for ultraviolet photodetection.

pmc-13541807.title: Effects of empagliflozin and metformin on biofilm formation and pathogenicity factors of urinary Escherichia coli isolates
pmc-13541807.creator: Aybala Temel, Ayşegül Ateş, Zinnet Şevval Aksoyalp
pmc-13541807.description: Escherichia coli, a major cause of urinary tract infections (UTIs), forms biofilms that contribute to antimicrobial resistance. Antidiabetic medications have gained attention for their potential antimicrobial effects, though data remain limited. This study investigated the inhibitory effects of empagliflozin and metformin against urinary E. coli isolates.

pmc-13552357.description: sed in our interviews, and in line with their findings, participants recognised its value in identifying blood vessels, selecting the optimal puncture site and informing decisions between percutaneous and surgical tracheostomy [2]. Participants in our study noted that ICU clinicians are proficient with ultrasound (for vascular access and point‐of‐care imaging) [2]. However, its application in PDT presents some challenges.
